scenes.line1: How do async queues boost reliability?
scenes.say: How do async queues make systems more reliable, and what happens when things fail?

scenes.label: Queues
scenes.sub: Decouple producers and consumers for background jobs.
scenes.say: Queues let you separate producers from consumers, so background jobs don't block your main flow.
With a queue, one worker handles each job. With publish-subscribe, every subscriber gets a copy of the message.

rows.b: If it fails, retry up to 3 times
Still fails? Move to dead-letter queue

scenes.say: If a job fails, retry it a few times. Still no luck? Send it to a dead-letter queue so it doesn't block everything else.

scenes.label: Idempotency
scenes.sub: Processing the same job twice is safe.
scenes.say: Idempotency means if you process the same job more than once, it won't break things.

scenes.question: What happens if you skip idempotency?
scenes.wrong: Jobs run faster with fewer checks.
scenes.right: You risk duplicate processing and data errors.
scenes.say: Don't skip idempotency. Without it, retries can cause duplicate work or bad data.
